text: Metropolitan Shio Mujiri - If we turn to the Lord for help, if our desire is genuine and strong, He will surely come with His grace, set us right, and cleanse us.

The Lord expects us to compel our soul, burdened and wounded by our sins, to turn to Him for salvation and mercy. Our correction, our inner transformation, can be accomplished only by God. We are unable to do this by our own strength,” said the Locum Tenens of the Patriarchal Throne, Metropolitan Shio of Senaki and Chkhorotsqu (Mujiri), during a sermon at the Holy Trinity Cathedral, where the Rite of the Deposition from the Cross was performed a short time ago.
According to Metropolitan Shio, “If our desire is genuine, strong, and serious, the Lord will certainly come with His grace, correct us, and cleanse us.”

“Through the glorious and ancient liturgical services of our Church, composed by the great holy fathers, renowned hymnographers, the finest poets, thinkers, and sages, we have the opportunity not only to learn from the Gospel the events related to the Lord Jesus Christ, but also, through the services, to become participants in those events. Therefore, today we have brought forth the Holy Shroud, and we are all participants in this event.”

Here gathered are those who are assembled—not those who were shouting just a short while ago, “Crucify him, crucify him,” but those who say to the Lord, “Forgive us, O Lord.” We have been instructed by the Church; we know the teaching of the Church, that by our sins we again and again crucify the Lord. He came to earth, became incarnate, suffered, and died in order to free us from the bondage of sin, from the burden of sin.

Who was the first person whom the Lord freed from this burden? — one of the crucified robbers, the wise robber, who, having so deeply felt the sufferings of the innocent Savior, confessed his sins and turned to the Savior in repentance from the cross. The Lord expects the same from us: that, burdened and wounded by our sins, we compel our soul to turn to God for salvation and mercy.

Many of us, and some even for years, try on our own to fix something in our souls, in our lives, without God, by our own strength. This is a futile attempt. It is only a proud, foolish attempt, because only God can correct us and bring about inner change. By our own strength, we cannot do this. We may be able to change our behavior slightly on the outside, but it is beyond our reach to be changed inwardly, as the Lord says, “Without Me you can do nothing.”

Dear brothers and sisters, the Lord desires our correction and purification. I would like to remind you of a time when a sick man came to Him and said, “Lord, if You are willing, You can cleanse me.” What did the Lord answer? — “I am willing; be cleansed.” This is what the Lord desires. The will of man and the will of God coincided, and that man was healed.

“So, our correction and purification are desired by the Lord even more than we desire them. If our desire is genuine, strong, and serious, and we turn to the Lord for help, He will surely come with His grace, correct us, and purify us. May God bless you and strengthen you. Let us pray to the Lord to grant us strength and help, so that we may walk in the path of truth, the path of light, and with Christ. Amen,” said Metropolitan Shio.
